Chapter 08 of 18

The Outer Circuit

Check The EdgeSeawall / West End / Stanley Park edge110 BPM
The story

The seawall looks like a path for walking and cycling. It is really the Outer Circuit, a perimeter inspection route, and its job is to check that Terminal City still meets the water in the correct place.

The inspectors are the walkers, runners, cyclists, and people who simply cannot sleep. Every one of them is verifying the edge of the city, whether they know it or not. This matters more than it sounds. If enough of them stop moving at once, sections of the shoreline begin to disagree about where they belong.

The Repair People inspect the cracks along the wall. Around Stanley Park the Green Static interrupts the Circuit's signals, and somewhere near Wreck Beach there may be a gap in it that nobody has closed: the Endless Stair. Keep moving. Water on the left. City on the right. Hold the edge.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
